reason: The cited evidence shows liquid-phase sintering and interphase formation in other diboride systems (E5, E1), but none involves a boron oxide/Si precursor forming a borosilicate interphase in ZrB2 at ~1650 °C. The specific claims about the precursor, the resulting borosilicate chemistry, and its protective functions against oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion are not directly supported by the cited passages.
premises: A boron oxide/Si precursor forms a transient liquid phase at ~1650 °C that promotes densification of ZrB2.
The liquid phase segregates to grain boundaries and solidifies as a continuous borosilicate interphase.
The borosilicate interphase impedes oxygen ingress and retards liquid metal penetration.
The in-situ formed interphase refines the microstructure and maintains mechanical strength.
Full densification and protective performance are achievable at ≤1700 °C processing and up to ~1600 °C service.
